claims.claim: SoundHound's June 30, 2026 10-Q shows acquisition-related capital and integration exposure beyond headline organic growth: the Interactions acquisition carried $76.1 million fair-value purchase consideration, including $19.4 million cash to sellers, $4.1 million seller transaction expenses, and repayment of $41.5 million of Interactions debt.

This creates a measurable execution test: acquired growth can strengthen distribution and capability, but durable value requires post-acquisition revenue, retention and margin contribution to exceed integration and capital costs rather than merely expanding reported scale.

causalEdges.from: acquisition capital and assumed debt repayment
causalEdges.mechanism: cash consideration, transaction expense and debt repayment raise the economic hurdle for acquired growth
causalEdges.falsifier: future filings show durable acquired-customer retention, improving consolidated margins and cash generation sufficient to demonstrate returns above acquisition/integration costs

risks.risk: Acquisition integration and capital deployment can obscure underlying unit economics if acquired revenue does not convert into durable margin and cash generation.

unknowns.unknown: Current evidence does not isolate full-cycle return on acquisition capital or retention economics for acquired customer cohorts.
